method: All four corrected PNGs individually opened with view_image at original detail; sky strips are six consecutive native-scale rows. Production application rendered with Playwright controlled browser clock, not state-only factory.
findings: Bird is clearly visible and progresses rightward at sampled 7,12,18 seconds in DPR 1 and DPR 2.
At 0/3.9 seconds bird is absent. At 4.5 seconds expected state has only just entered and its body is not clearly distinguishable; this is not claimed as visual entry proof.
Airplanes and drifting cloud are present; sampled bird is separated vertically from airplanes.
Pause with reduced motion gave exact RGBA equality after 2 seconds; resume reached running state; no browser page errors.
Resize produced native canvas 900x700 in both DPR cases; visual resize adoption is not claimed.
limitations: Browser time was advanced with Playwright clock; this is not wall-clock or every-frame observation.
Full exit and subsequent flight cycle were not visually verified.
Expected geometry/state metadata is calculated; exact rendered pixel position was not measured.
Finite samples do not prove continuous cloud or aircraft separation at all times.
